event_text: American Revolutionary War: The Royal Navy defeats the Penobscot Expedition with the most significant loss of United States naval forces prior to the attack on Pearl Harbor.
headline: Britain Delivers Crushing Blow to American Naval Forces at Penobscot Bay
story: Barry and Susan perched on a mast, watching the chaos unfold below. 'Looks like the Royal Navy's got the upper hand, Susan,' Barry said, fluffing his feathers. 'The Penobscot Expedition, meant to be a show of force by the Americans, has turned into a bit of a debacle. Commodore Dudley Saltonstall's fleet is outnumbered and outgunned, and those British ships are making short work of them.' Susan cocked her head to one side. 'I count 19 American vessels, Barry. All either sunk or captured. Not exactly the most auspicious start to their naval endeavors.' Barry nodded, eyeing the destruction. 'And the Brits? Just one ship damaged. Makes you wonder why the Americans even bothered, doesn't it? I mean, 470 American sailors and troops either killed, wounded, or taken prisoner. Quite the reversal of fortunes.'
regret_line: One might think they'd regret underestimating the Royal Navy, but hindsight's always 20/20, isn't it?
winner_line: The British shipbuilding industry, which no doubt received a nice boost in orders after this little demonstration of superiority.
